statutoryTitle: Decision of the European Central Bank of 19 April 2013 (ECB/2013/10)
subtitle: On the denominations, specifications, reproduction, exchange and withdrawal of euro banknotes

articles.heading: Exchange of mutilated or damaged euro banknotes
articles.statutoryText:
1. National Central Banks (NCBs) shall exchange mutilated or damaged genuine legal tender euro banknotes where:
(a) more than 50% of the banknote surface area is presented; or
(b) 50% or less of the banknote is presented, if the applicant proves that the missing parts have been destroyed.

2. For the purposes of paragraph 1, NCBs shall charge a fee where euro banknotes have been mutilated or damaged as a result of anti-theft devices, or where an applicant submits 100 or more mutilated or damaged euro banknotes.

3. Where NCBs know or have sufficient reason to believe that a criminal offence has been committed, they shall refuse to exchange the damaged euro banknotes and shall hand them over to the competent authorities.

overFiftyPercent.authority: All Eurosystem National Central Bank counters (Bundesbank, Banque de France, Banca d'Italia, Banco de España, etc.) and commercial retail banks.

subFiftyPercent.authority: NCB Central Cash Offices upon submission of sworn destruction certificate and forensic inspection.

technicalStandards.substrate: Pure 100% cotton fiber with embedded polyvinyl alcohol sizing.
opticalSecurityFeatures: Portrait Hologram Window with Satellite Kinegram
technicalStandards.counterProcedures: Commercial credit institutions are required to accept damaged notes for forwarding or credit under Article 6 of Regulation (EC) No 1338/2001.
